metadata.title: Inside Data Collection Factories: Why Robot Data Is So Scarce | Robotics Series
metadata.guest_role: Robot data platforms · teleop factories · Agibot context

conclusion: What robotics envies most about LLMs is data. Host Chen Qian flies to Shanghai teleop factories to show why embodiment data is not on the internet: every high-quality trajectory must be produced. A four-layer pyramid (internet video → mocap → teleop → robot-self) is skewed — teleop may be ~1/10,000 of the pool yet decides real-world success. Sim-to-real and embodiment gaps block cheap scaling; China answers with labor-efficient data factories while Valley bets platforms. Agibot hitting 10k embodied units is volume, not yet the data key.
background: Robotics series episode after dexterous hands and open/closed models. Guests from Sharpa and Mifeng discuss Tacmap-style tactile sim bridges, 100k–1M hour customer asks, and why human teleoperators cannot feel what the robot feels.
important_facts: DeepMind RT-1 lore: 13 robots collecting for 17 months in office/kitchen — still tiny vs LLM scrapes. Teleop is hard because operators lack robot proprioception/tactile feedback; mocap/YouTube miss robot-state. Mifeng pitches physical-AI data infra: ~2M teleop hours capacity in 2026 plus ~8M hours planned other paradigms.

Gaps: Sim-to-Real (physics/contact mismatch), Embodiment Gap (human hand ≠ robot hand; occlusion corrupts state), Functional Retargeting (copying motion shape ≠ task intent). Tacmap translates fingertip deformation maps to help fine skills but inherits sim gaps. For complex tasks, trajectory ratios ~ teleop:mocap:web ≈ 1:100:10000 — quality over raw hours.

Strategy split: Chinese OEMs industrialize teleop labor into factories as a moat; Valley faces expensive labor so pushes simulation and platformization. Goals differ — industrial 100% success vs consumer generalization with human handoff — so data mixes differ. Agibot claimed 10k embodied robots by late March; data key still open.

mental_model.name: Data Pyramid × Teleop Scarcity × Factory vs Platform
mental_model.components: Rank data by embodiment fidelity; accept that the rarest teleop slice unlocks deployment; choose China-style labor factories or Valley-style sim/platforms based on wage and goal (yield vs generality).
mental_model.application: Diligence robotics on who owns teleop capacity and quality pipelines, not only model demos. GOOGL/DeepMind RT history shows even giants under-collect. Prefer integrators that treat data ops as product.

key_insights.view: Robot scaling is blocked by a data desert, not FLOPs alone.
key_insights.question: Why can't LLMs' web scrape transfer?
key_insights.answer: Internet has human video, not robot-on-task state with force/tactile loops.

key_insights.question: Why not just scale YouTube?
key_insights.answer: Pyramid ratios bury teleop, but real contact success still hinges on it.

key_insights.view: China's edge may be data factories.
key_insights.question: What's the moat?
key_insights.answer: Cheap, organized teleop labor + full-stack collection vs Valley's sim-heavy path.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Data infra/teleop capacity is the scarce layer under humanoid hype — early, low
Episode guest path on tactile/sim translation; pre-scale — low
DeepMind RT collection history shows infra advantage; not a pure robot pure-play — low

golden_quotes: We have no data for training robots.
